newsitem.title: USA: Spielberg's "Jurassic" sequel enjoys bronto opening.
newsitem.headline: Spielberg's "Jurassic" sequel enjoys bronto opening.

text.p: Steven Spielberg's dinosaurs trampled box office records during Memorial Day weekend as "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" opened with an estimated $85.7 million for the four-day period, according to studio estimates issued on Monday.
The special effects extravaganza kicked off a busy summer movie season full of mega-budgeted releases by establishing a slew of new benchmarks.
Its four-day total beats the previous record held by "Mission: Impossible," which earned $56.8 million when it opened during the Memorial Day holiday last year.
Its three-day total (Friday to Sunday) of $69.1 million beats the $52.78 million that 1995's "Batman Forever" earned during its first three days.
Additionally, the film's $22 million opening on Friday beat the $20.1 million opening for "Batman Forever."

"The Lost World: Jurassic Park" features Jeff Goldblum, returning from the 1993 original, Julianne Moore, Vince Vaughn and Pete Postlethwaite, who battle raging raptors and evil capitalists in a loose adaptation of novelist Michael Crichton's "The Lost World." But the real stars are the dinosaurs -- bigger, faster and hungrier than before -- and the film's special effects team.
Carrying a reported budget of $80 million, a bargain by the standards of other movies on the summer slate, the film is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Canada's Seagram Co. Ltd..
